first_impression.reaction: Googled 'mykonos wedding' because it's on the list next to Santorini. The intro gives me three decisions in order instead of a party-island sales pitch, so I kept going. Jumped to the FAQ and the cost section first, as always. No numbers in the cost section, but it names real catches: Saint John's planner-arranged extras come 'with additional charges', and capacity changes shape at 60 versus 120 at Mykonos Blu. The weather table admits there's no station on Mykonos, and the travel section tells me about heatwaves, wildfires, earthquakes and ferries cancelled in wind. That's not a business hiding the catch. My gripes: two different names for the concierge service, a couple of 'many couples' lines, one FAQ answer that dodges the yes or no, and one line that drifts into brochure talk.

journey.quote: A Mykonos wedding comes down to three decisions, made in order: whether the ceremony is legal or symbolic, which starts the paperwork clock; the season, read from official climate figures and current travel advice; and the area and kind of venue that suit your guest list.
journey.reaction: A sequence I can turn into spreadsheet columns. No one's tried to sell me a beach club yet.

journey.quote: A legal ceremony is one of your two routes.
journey.reaction: I asked whether you can legally get married there. That's not a yes or a no. The answer is probably yes, so say yes, then give me the 'check with the municipality' part.

journey.quote: An overseas marriage cannot be registered in Australia, so a legal step at home keeps the paperwork simple.
journey.reaction: Read on its own, this makes it sound like a Greek marriage wouldn't count back home. The body says it's usually recognised, just not registered here. The FAQ is the bit I read first, so it should say both halves.

journey.quote: Many couples complete the legal step in Australia, then hold a symbolic ceremony on the island.
journey.reaction: 'Many' compared to what? Probably true, but it's the word I'd test. 'Some couples' says the same thing without the claim.

journey.section: What shapes the cost of a Mykonos wedding
journey.quote: At Mykonos Blu, the ceremony balcony holds up to 60 while the restaurant and pool area holds up to 120, so a larger party means a different ceremony plan.
journey.reaction: A real constraint with real numbers against a named venue. That's what I want in a cost section, even with no prices.

journey.section: House rules to agree before you book
journey.quote: Saint John works with experienced wedding planners for flowers, DJs, photography and fireworks, with additional charges.
journey.reaction: There's the catch, named. Good to know before I start comparing quotes.

journey.section: Weather by month at Naxos, the nearest official weather station
journey.quote: The figures below are for Naxos, the nearest official weather station, so read them as a guide to the neighbouring Cyclades rather than a forecast for your venue.
journey.reaction: Upfront about the limits of its own data, with the rain days in a table. Most sites would just slap 'Mykonos weather' on it.

journey.quote: As at November 2026, [Smartraveller's advice for Greece](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/europe/greece) is to exercise normal safety precautions.
journey.reaction: Dated and from the government. Then it goes on about wildfires and earthquakes. A wedding business warning me about its own destination earns a point.

journey.section: Areas of the island and what each suits
journey.quote: **The sunset coast** suits couples who want the light to do the work.
journey.reaction: Every other line in this section is a beach name or a venue. This one is a mood. I skip mood.

journey.section: Five venues to start your shortlist
journey.quote: These are examples across the settings above, not a ranking.
journey.reaction: 'Not a ranking' is the right thing to say. Though none of the five is in Hora and none is a private villa, so 'across the settings above' is a bit generous. Minor.

journey.section: Five venues to start your shortlist
journey.quote: The hotel describes its weddings as running from intimate gatherings to large weddings with up to 800 guests, from welcome cocktails to five-course gala dinners.
journey.reaction: 'The hotel describes' tells me whose claim it is. That's how to handle a big number.

journey.section: Choosing where to marry on Mykonos
journey.quote: Once you have an area and a style in mind, [talk to Wonderland Concierge]
journey.reaction: The closing section calls it 'Wedded Concierge'. Two names for the same service on one page? Either it's sloppy or they're two different things, and either way I'm now wondering which one I'd be paying.

journey.section: Choosing where to marry on Mykonos
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor is a single point of contact, start to finish, and confirms the unpublished details above and every inclusion in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Mid-page CTA, but it lands after a fair amount of evidence and promises something specific. Doesn't make me click yet, doesn't annoy me either.

journey.section: House rules to agree before you book
journey.quote: Get the answers in the contract or a written confirmation, not a chat thread.
journey.reaction: Someone who's seen a vendor walk back a WhatsApp promise. I'm sending this whole list of questions to every venue.

journey.quote: The fee is agreed in writing before any work begins, and every inclusion is confirmed in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Right signal. Still doesn't tell me whether you take a cut from the venues, but a fee agreed up front beats one buried in supplier quotes.

unanswered_questions: Are 'Wonderland Concierge' and 'Wedded Concierge' the same service?
Does Wedded Wonderland take a commission or mark-up from any of these venues?
How is the Wedded Concierge fee worked out, and what does it cover?
Where a venue like Saint John uses its own planners for extras, does Wedded Concierge replace them or sit on top of them?
Is there a real Mykonos wedding with the actual budget I can look at?

turn_offs_found.quote: **The sunset coast** suits couples who want the light to do the work.
turn_offs_found.why: The rest of the area guide gives me places and venues. This line gives me a feeling, and feelings are what I discount when I'm comparing three planners side by side.

turn_offs_found.quote: Many couples sign the legal paperwork quietly in Australia, then hold the full ceremony on Mykonos with nothing left to file.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Many' is a claim about other people's behaviour stated as fact, with nothing behind it. 'Some couples' costs nothing and doesn't make me wonder where the number came from. Same for the FAQ line 'Many couples complete the legal step in Australia'.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the 'House rules to agree before you book' questions, to send to every venue on our list
Both sets of parents: the flying, ferry and heat sections, so they know about stairs, wind and summer heat

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [plan your Mykonos wedding with a Wedded Advisor]
cta_reaction.why: The page earned it: dated travel advice, honest weather data, real venue catches, and a question list I'll actually use. The CTAs come after evidence and don't oversell. What holds me back is the usual: do you take a cut, and how is the fee worked out? And the 'Wonderland Concierge' versus 'Wedded Concierge' slip made me pause before clicking.

top_3_changes: Fix the service name in the mid-page CTA: 'talk to Wonderland Concierge' should match 'Wedded Concierge' used in the closing section, so it doesn't read as two different services.

Tighten the FAQ: open 'Can you legally get married in Mykonos?' with a straight yes before 'check with the municipality', and rewrite the symbolic-ceremony answer so it says an overseas marriage is usually recognised in Australia but can't be registered here, rather than implying it doesn't count.

Cut the brochure and 'many' lines: drop 'who want the light to do the work' (just say the sunset coast suits a sunset ceremony), and change 'Many couples' to 'Some couples' in both the legal section and the FAQ. (Commission, fee model and a free first call would also help, but those are deferred business details, so nice-to-have.)

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Daniel (sceptic): FAQ and costs first, looked for catches, superlatives, fee model and commissions
No invented brand facts; commission, fee model, planner overlap, first call and naming question placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (image slots, fact tags, CTA markers) ignored
Title, deferred business details and absence of prices not flagged as must-fix; no requests for sourcing or 'not published' explanations

open_questions.question: The mid-page CTA says 'Wonderland Concierge' while the closing says 'Wedded Concierge' (the brand term). This looks like a copy slip rather than a deferred business detail; please confirm it is in scope as a must-fix.

assumptions: Daniel arrived via a Google search for 'mykonos wedding' with Mykonos on the shortlist while comparing three planners.
No prices on the page, including the cost section, is by design and not penalised.
Title is person-set and deferred, so not assessed.
